title: A clue inside a fossil
hook: Some fossils preserve traces of feeding.

knows: Animals can leave traces of their activity.
doesNotKnow: Use contents of an identified coprolite without overstating producer identity.

misconception: A fossil dropping always identifies its maker and whole diet.
objective: Use contents of an identified coprolite without overstating producer identity.

claims.text: Some fossils preserve traces of feeding. An independently identified fossil dropping contains identifiable plant fragments. What can these fragments support? The schematic shows plant fragments in an identified fossil dropping. If those fragments are correctly identified, they support the presence of plant material in that dropping. They do not by themselves identify the producer or every meal it ate.
claims.source: Source lead for independent checking: Smithsonian https://naturalhistory.si.edu/collections/paleobiology. Identification of both dropping and fragments is stipulated in the example.

claims.text: The schematic figure and its chosen timing, species or measurements represent the explicitly stated example and are not photographic evidence of an individual specimen.
claims.source: Simplified schematic; constructed example where indicated.

claims.text: Recall: An identified fossil dropping contains fish fragments. What can the fragments support? Identified contents support that content, not a complete diet or producer identity.
